title: Empirical Bayes as named prior-from-the-data shrinkage
dek: Wikipedia EB: estimate the prior from the ensemble, then shrink. Not fully Bayesian, not a p-value. Catalogue screens love it.
story: Empirical Bayes on Wikipedia estimates the prior (or hyperprior) from the same ensemble you will shrink, then pretends that prior was known. It is a two-step that often works for many parallel units (genes, schools, SNPs, isolates' random effects).
It is not a full posterior over the prior (that would be hierarchical Bayes with uncertainty in τ). SEs that ignore the estimation of τ are too small.
stats-partial-pooling is the GLM version. Storey π0 is an EB flavour for p-values (stats-fdr).
deep: If the ensemble is one scientific object (one new drug), EB has nothing to estimate.
Tweedie's formula is a named EB celebrity for exponential families.
Selection (only report the big hits) without a selective-inference repair wrecks EB.
Do not call EB a p-value correction.

visual.caption: Ensemble in, estimate G, shrink units. Uncertainty in G is the part people forget to carry.
